text:
Lina: Heads-up — spotted a routing mismatch in the canary for tenant routing. Some mobile clients are getting sent to our Dedicated pool even though they should hit hosted. Not sure if UA or custom header precedence is wrong.

anil: Can you paste a sample request and the route decision log?

Lina: Paste from the edge log: 
```
headers: {
  'x-signed-assertion': null,
  'x-customer-id': 'acct-42',
  'user-agent': 'RedwoodMobile/3.2.1 (iOS)'
}
route_decision: "matched: user-agent -> dedicated"
```
Seems the UA rule won even though we expected x-customer-id to dominate.

megan: That sounds like a precedence bug. Our intended order is: signed assertion (if present & valid) -> x-customer-id (explicit tenant header) -> user-agent heuristics -> default.

Lina: Exactly. The route config currently looks like this in the console rule:
```yaml
match:
  - header_equals:
      x-signed-assertion: present
  - header_equals:
      x-customer-id: present
  - header_regex:
      user-agent: ".*RedwoodMobile.*"
actions:
  route: dedicated
  require_signature: false
```
So `require_signature` is false which lets UA match even when we expected x-customer-id to win.

megan: Big :yikes:. If require_signature is false we intentionally fall through and allow less-specific matches. For tenant routing we should default require_signature: true. Otherwise spoofing is trivial.

priya: Also telemetry gap — we currently only emit a single counter "route_match" with route name. We need a per-matcher label (signature|tenant-header|ua-heuristic) so we can detect how many decisions are relying on heuristics.

anil: Agreed. Proposal: change route matching precedence to be explicit (scored matcher) and introduce a "match_source" label emitted to tracing/metrics. Pseudo-config: 
```yaml
match_strategy: prioritized
matchers:
  - id: signed_assertion
    type: header_exists
    header: x-signed-assertion
    require_signature: true
  - id: tenant_header
    type: header_equals
    header: x-customer-id
  - id: ua_mobile
    type: regex
    header: user-agent
    pattern: ".*RedwoodMobile.*"
```
This makes the choice deterministic and easier to reason about.

megan: We also need to validate signatures upstream (verify signer, expiry). If signed_assertion is present but invalid we should emit a separate metric `routing.signature_invalid` and fall through to tenant_header rather than UA.

Lina: Good call. Concern: what about proxies that re-add x-customer-id incorrectly? We should enforce an x-route-signer header (internal) that only our gateway can inject before routing. If present, treat x-customer-id as authoritative.

anil: That fits. Add a small rule: if x-route-signer == "edge-gateway" then tenant_header gets a higher priority score.

priya: For the console UX change: add a "Test request" button on the route detail page that shows which matcher fired and the metric labels that a sample request would emit. That will make rollouts safer.

megan: Ops implications: quota/accounting currently attributed by route only. If we start routing more via tenant_header we need to ensure quota lookup happens using the authoritative tenant id (not UA). Edge case: if tenant_header absent and we fall back to UA we should apply a reduced quota or raise an audit event.

Lina: Proposed action items: 
- Patch canary route: set require_signature: true for tenant-sensitive routes (megan)
- Add match_source label to routing metrics and tracing (priya)
- Implement signature validation with invalid_signature counter (anil)
- Add x-route-signer check + console test UX (megan + devex)
I'll open PRs and link them here.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-18T14:27:12Z finished for canary/routing-rules v2.1 — 3/3 pods healthy.

ops-bot: metric created: routing.match_source (labels: route, match_source, tenant_id) and routing.signature_invalid.counter initialized.

Lina: Thanks all — once PRs are up I will run a targeted canary against tenant-42 and watch match_source counts. If we see >1% heuristic matches after the patch, hold rollout. :thumbsup:

anil: Will add the unit test that simulates proxy-rewrite where x-customer-id is forged; test ensures x-route-signer absent -> tenant_header deprioritized.

priya: I'll wire the new labels into the per-route dashboard and add an alert for "heuristic_match_rate > 0.5%" for tenant routes.

megan: Sounds good. Thanks — great catch, Lina.
